subject: MAP: performance benchmarking plan, workload profiles & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Elena Garcia <elena@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Performance benchmarks & close timeline for Acme pilot

Hi Vivek / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we align our MAP and procurement timeline, we need a concrete benchmarking plan for the pilot to sign-off on acceptance criteria and associated close milestones. High-level ask:

- Define workload profiles (interactive chat, bulk embeddings, batched inference) and expected concurrency slices.
- Provide clear SLOs: TTFT (95th/99th), token throughput, sustained concurrency, and error-rate ceilings.
- Describe test methodology (cold vs warm starts, KV cache warmup, prefix caching), required artifacts (scripts, harness), and expected run duration.
- Target date: we'd like acceptance criteria finalized by Oct 20 so procurement can include the performance milestones in the SOW.

For Acme: target production-like shape is ~400-600 concurrent interactive users (peaks), target P95 TTFT <= 2.5s for short chat prompts (<=256 tokens), sustained throughput target ~60k tokens/min across the cluster, and less than 0.5% server errors during steady-state. We understand you may propose different slices and we welcome your recommendations.

Can you share a proposed test matrix and a tentative calendar (when you can run tests and when we can review results)? Also please include artifacts we need to provide (sample prompts, access controls, any infra requirements).

Thanks,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa, Karthik and Irene to scope. Initial proposal below; attaching two artifacts (llm-load-profiles.csv, test-harness-readme.md).

Proposed test scope (summary):
- Workload slices:
  1) Interactive chat (short prompts <=256 tokens) — primary SLO: P95 TTFT
  2) Conversational long context (<=2k tokens) — measure P95/P99 latency and memory/kv usage
  3) Bulk embeddings (batched) — throughput (tokens/sec and ops/sec)
  4) Ramp & endurance (sustained 4h run at target concurrency)

- Acceptance SLOs (proposal):
  * Interactive P95 TTFT <= 2.4s; P99 <= 4.0s
  * Sustained throughput target within +/-10% of baseline profile (we'll define baseline tokens/min)
  * Error rate < 0.5% (5xx responses or timeouts)
  * Successful run defined as passing >= 90% of sample prompts with stable output latency and no safety regressions (semantic checks handled separately)

- Test methodology highlights:
  * Define cold vs warm measurements — cold = first-token after a long idle period, warm = after KV/prefix warming with representative traffic for 30 minutes
  * KV cache warm-up: we will run a 20-minute warm-up trace derived from your sample prompt set prior to TTFT measurement
  * Concurrency ramp: 0 -> target over 10 minutes, steady-state for the configured window (10–60 minutes depending on slice)

- Infrastructure notes: we plan to run on a dedicated Redwood pool (us-west2 GPUs), require an S3 bucket for logs and a service account for temporary test tokens.

Proposed calendar:
- Draft test matrix & acceptance criteria delivered by EOD Thu Oct 15
- Test run window: Oct 18–19 (we can provision multiple runs)
- Results review & sign-off call: Oct 19 or Oct 20 (your preference)

Please review the attached CSV (llm-load-profiles.csv) — it contains candidate concurrency/sequence-length mixes. We'll refine after Marissa and Karthik add thresholds and measurement details.

-vivek

Quick version of the acceptance checklist and SLO definitions — putting these here so they land in the MAP document. Attaching acceptance-checklist.xlsx with a per-slice checklist.

SLOs and pass/fail rules (detailed):
- Interactive chat (slice A):
  * P95 TTFT <= 2.4s (pass if P95 across 3 runs <= 2.4s)
  * P99 TTFT <= 4.0s (soft threshold; flag for investigation if >4.0s)
  * Error rate < 0.5% (5xx or gateway errors counted)
  * Latency jitter: stddev(P95 across runs) < 15%

- Long context (slice B):
  * P95 <= 3.5s, P99 <= 6.0s
  * Memory pressure observed — if OOMs or restarts occur, fail and require config change

- Bulk embeddings (slice C):
  * Throughput >= baseline_tokens_per_min * 0.9 across a 30-minute sustained run
  * Percent CUDA utilization within expected range (we'll capture GPU metrics)

Measurement rules:
- Each slice will be executed 3 times (independent runs) and we report median and variance.
- TTFT definition: time from request submission to first token emitted by the model. For streaming we measure first-byte latency.
- Warm vs cold: report both; primary acceptance based on warm measurements.

Artifacts required from Acme:
- Representative prompt corpus (redacted) for interactive and long-context slices
- Expected tokenization rules / any custom pre/post-processing
- Approval for Redwood test service account and S3 write access (logs + metrics)

I'll align the acceptance-checklist sheet with your procurement items so this can be referenced from the SOW.

Adding the technical test-plan details and runbook notes. Attached: load-scripts.tar.gz (contains JMeter/Locust derivative and Redwood harness glue).

Run design (technical):
- Environment: Redwood dedicated pool (r5-like instances for control plane; A100-equivalent for model serving). We will pin model version provided by Acme or use Redwood-verified equivalent.
- Metrics to capture:
  * request_id, trace_id, first_token_latency_ms, total_tokens, model_version, host_id, gpu_util_pct, mem_free_mb, error_code
  * Prometheus + traces collected, logs to S3, results summarized to a CSV per run
- Cold-start measurement: spin new container / empty KV then fire a fixed set of 200 unique prompts (measured per container). Repeat across 5 containers.
- Warm measurement: after 20-minute warm-up, run 3 independent steady-state runs for 15 minutes each, with concurrency profile from the CSV.
- Concurrency ramp: linear ramp from 1 to target concurrency across 10 minutes; then steady-state window.

Important measurement notes (TTFT/concurrency interplay):
- TTFT will be captured at both client-side and server-side to detect network vs compute bottlenecks.
- We'll run microbenchmarks for kernel-level perf if we see unexpected P99 spikes (collect perf counters).
- For long-context tests we will vary sequence length (512, 1024, 2048) to observe non-linear scaling.

Schedule ask: please confirm access to the sample prompt corpus and approve the service account by EOD Fri Oct 16 so we can run tests Oct 18. If procurement needs performance milestones in the SOW earlier, we can run a smaller synthetic run this week for a preliminary data point.

-karthik

Vivek / team — this looks good and addresses most of our concerns. A few clarifications before we finalize the MAP:

1) Procurement needs a short summary line for the SOW: please provide a one-paragraph acceptance statement we can paste in (we'll need that by Oct 18).
2) For the warm-up procedure: confirm you will use the same sample corpus that we provide (we will sanitize and send by Tue Oct 15).
3) Can you confirm whether the 20-minute warm-up will be sufficient for KV cache at the concurrency we specified? If not, suggest alternatives.

Samir and I are OK with the Oct 18–19 run window; schedule a results review call on Mon Oct 19 at 10:00 AM PT and include a 30-minute buffer for walkthrough. If you prefer Oct 20, procurement will push the SOW to the following week which is less ideal for us.

We will upload the prompt corpus to the shared drive and grant the service account by EOD Oct 16. Procurement asks that the one-paragraph acceptance line explicitly reference P95 TTFT and the sustained throughput baseline.

Thanks — Elena
